findings.title: Session-like cookie 'PHPSESSID' lacks HttpOnly
findings.why: Any XSS can read the cookie and hijack the session.

findings.title: Cookie 'PHPSESSID' lacks Secure flag
findings.why: The cookie can be sent over plain HTTP and sniffed or injected.

findings.title: Cookie 'tracking' uses SameSite=None without Secure
findings.why: Browsers reject SameSite=None cookies that are not Secure.

findings.title: CORS wildcard origin combined with credentials
findings.why: Browsers reject this pair, but it signals a misconfigured policy that may be 'fixed' by reflecting any Origin.
findings.fix: Use an explicit origin allow-list; never reflect arbitrary Origin with credentials.

findings.title: CSP script-src allows 'unsafe-eval'
findings.why: eval()-style execution is permitted, enabling several XSS gadgets.
findings.fix: Remove 'unsafe-eval' and refactor code that needs eval/new Function.

findings.title: CSP script-src allows 'unsafe-inline'
findings.why: Inline scripts run, which defeats most of CSP's XSS protection.
findings.fix: Use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'.

findings.title: CSP script-src uses overly broad source (https:)
findings.why: Scripts can be loaded from any matching origin, including attacker-controlled ones.
findings.fix: List specific trusted hosts or use nonces with 'strict-dynamic'.

findings.title: No clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.why: The page can be framed by any site and used for clickjacking.

findings.title: Session-like cookie 'PHPSESSID' lacks SameSite
findings.why: Relies on browser defaults (Lax) for CSRF protection; older browsers differ.

findings.title: Session-like cookie '__Host-auth' lacks SameSite
findings.why: Relies on browser defaults (Lax) for CSRF protection; older browsers differ.

findings.title: Cookie 'theme' lacks Secure flag
findings.why: The cookie can be sent over plain HTTP and sniffed or injected.

findings.title: Cookie 'tracking' lacks Secure flag
findings.why: The cookie can be sent over plain HTTP and sniffed or injected.

findings.title: Cookie '__Host-auth' violates __Host- prefix rules
findings.why: __Host- requires Secure, Path=/ and no Domain; browsers drop the cookie otherwise.
findings.fix: Fix the attributes or drop the prefix.

findings.title: CSP lacks base-uri
findings.why: Injected <base> tags could redirect relative URLs.

findings.title: x-powered-by header reveals technology
findings.why: Reveals the stack/version to attackers.

findings.title: Server header discloses a version
findings.why: Exact versions help attackers match known CVEs.
findings.fix: Remove the version (e.g. ServerTokens Prod / server_tokens off).

findings.title: HSTS max-age is short (300 s)
findings.why: A short window leaves users unprotected once it expires.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
findings.why: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses, which can turn uploads/JSON into executable content.

findings.title: Cookie 'theme' lacks HttpOnly
findings.why: Name does not look like a session cookie; JS access may be intended. Verify.
findings.fix: Add HttpOnly if client scripts do not need it.

findings.title: Cookie 'tracking' lacks HttpOnly
findings.why: Name does not look like a session cookie; JS access may be intended. Verify.
findings.fix: Add HttpOnly if client scripts do not need it.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.why: Powerful browser features are not explicitly restricted.
findings.fix: Add e.g. Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.why: Modern browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, so impact is small.

not_flagged.reason: CSRF/XSRF token cookies are intentionally readable by JavaScript (double-submit pattern).
